title: Alternating Current
syllabus: Alternating currents, peak and RMS value of alternating current/voltage; Reactance and impedance; LCR series circuit, resonance; Quality factor, power in AC circuits, wattless current; AC generator and transformer

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] In a series LCR circuit, the values of inductance, capacitance, and resistance are $L = 10\text{ mH}$, $C = 1\,\mu\text{F}$, and $R = 100\,\Omega$ respectively. The resonance frequency $\nu_0$ of the circuit is:
questions.solution:
Resonance frequency is given by:
$$\nu_0 = \frac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{LC}}$$
Substitute $L = 10 \times 10^{-3}\text{ H} = 10^{-2}\text{ H}$ and $C = 10^{-6}\text{ F}$:
$$\sqrt{LC} = \sqrt{10^{-2} \times 10^{-6}} = \sqrt{10^{-8}} = 10^{-4}\text{ s}$$
$$\nu_0 = \frac{1}{2\pi \times 10^{-4}} = \frac{10^4}{2\pi} = \frac{10000}{6.283} \approx 1591.5\text{ Hz} \approx 1.59\text{ kHz}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] An alternating current is given by $I = I_1\cos(\omega t) + I_2\sin(\omega t)$. The RMS value of this current is:
questions.solution:
The peak amplitude of the sinusoidal current is:
$$I_0 = \sqrt{I_1^2 + I_2^2}$$
RMS current for a pure sinusoidal waveform is:
$$I_{\text{rms}} = \frac{I_0}{\sqrt{2}} = \frac{\sqrt{I_1^2 + I_2^2}}{\sqrt{2}} = \sqrt{\frac{I_1^2 + I_2^2}{2}}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] In a series LCR circuit at resonance, the phase difference between the applied alternating voltage and the resulting alternating current is:
questions.solution:
Phase angle $\phi$ in a series LCR circuit satisfies:
$$\tan\phi = \frac{X_L - X_C}{R}$$
At resonance, inductive reactance equals capacitive reactance ($X_L = X_C$), so:
$$\tan\phi = 0 \implies \phi = 0$$
Voltage and current are in phase.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] A step-down transformer transforms $2200\text{ V}$ to $220\text{ V}$. If the primary coil has 2000 turns and efficiency of the transformer is $90\%$, the number of turns in the secondary coil is:
questions.solution:
Turn ratio relation for a transformer:
$$\frac{V_s}{V_p} = \frac{N_s}{N_p}$$
Turns in secondary:
$$N_s = N_p \left(\frac{V_s}{V_p}\right) = 2000 \times \left(\frac{220}{2200}\right) = 2000 \times \frac{1}{10} = 200$$
Note: Number of turns depends strictly on the induced EMF ratio per turn, unaffected by power efficiency.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2019] In a circuit, the alternating voltage and current are given by $V = 100\sin(100t)\text{ V}$ and $I = 100\sin\left(100t + \frac{\pi}{3}\right)\text{ mA}$. The average power dissipated in the circuit is:
questions.solution:
Peak values: $V_0 = 100\text{ V}$, $I_0 = 100\text{ mA} = 0.1\text{ A}$.
Phase difference: $\phi = \pi/3$.
Average power in an AC circuit:
$$P_{\text{avg}} = V_{\text{rms}} I_{\text{rms}} \cos\phi = \left(\frac{V_0}{\sqrt{2}}\right) \left(\frac{I_0}{\sqrt{2}}\right) \cos\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right) = \frac{V_0 I_0}{2} \times \frac{1}{2}$$
$$P_{\text{avg}} = \frac{100 \times 0.1}{4} = \frac{10}{4} = 2.5\text{ W}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] The Quality factor ($Q$) of a series LCR resonant circuit with parameters $L, C,$ and $R$ is expressed as:
questions.solution:
Quality factor measures sharpness of resonance:
$$Q = \frac{\omega_0 L}{R} = \frac{1}{\omega_0 C R}$$
Since $\omega_0 = \frac{1}{\sqrt{LC}}$:
$$Q = \frac{1}{\sqrt{LC}}\frac{L}{R} = \frac{1}{R}\sqrt{\frac{L}{C}}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] An AC voltage source $V = V_0\sin(\omega t)$ is connected across a pure capacitor of capacitance $C$. The current $I(t)$ flowing in the circuit is:
questions.solution:
For a pure capacitor: $q(t) = C V(t) = C V_0\sin(\omega t)$.
$$I(t) = \frac{dq}{dt} = \omega C V_0\cos(\omega t) = \omega C V_0\sin\left(\omega t + \frac{\pi}{2}\right)$$
Current leads the voltage by a phase angle of $\pi/2$.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] A series LCR circuit has $R = 40\,\Omega$, inductive reactance $X_L = 100\,\Omega$, and capacitive reactance $X_C = 70\,\Omega$. The impedance of the circuit is:
questions.solution:
Impedance of a series LCR circuit:
$$Z = \sqrt{R^2 + (X_L - X_C)^2}$$
$$Z = \sqrt{40^2 + (100 - 70)^2} = \sqrt{40^2 + 30^2} = \sqrt{1600 + 900} = \sqrt{2500} = 50\,\Omega$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] The wattless component of current in an AC circuit carrying RMS current $I_{\text{rms}}$ with a phase angle $\phi$ between voltage and current is:
questions.solution:
The current can be resolved into two orthogonal components with respect to voltage:
1) $I_{\text{rms}}\cos\phi$ in phase with voltage, responsible for active power dissipation.
2) $I_{\text{rms}}\sin\phi$ in quadrature ($90^\circ$) with voltage, which consumes zero net power and is termed wattless current.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] In an AC circuit, an inductor of inductance $L$ and a resistor of resistance $R$ are connected in series across an AC source of angular frequency $\omega$. The power factor of the circuit is:
questions.solution:
Power factor is $\cos\phi = \frac{R}{Z}$.
For a series LR circuit, impedance is $Z = \sqrt{R^2 + X_L^2} = \sqrt{R^2 + \omega^2 L^2}$.
$$\cos\phi = \frac{R}{\sqrt{R^2 + \omega^2 L^2}}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2019] If the frequency of an alternating current supply is doubled, the inductive reactance $X_L$ and capacitive reactance $X_C$ will change respectively to:
questions.solution:
Inductive reactance: $X_L = 2\pi f L \implies X_L \propto f$. Doubling $f$ doubles $X_L$ to $2X_L$.
Capacitive reactance: $X_C = \frac{1}{2\pi f C} \implies X_C \propto \frac{1}{f}$. Doubling $f$ halves $X_C$ to $\frac{X_C}{2}$.

questions.question: A capacitor blocks direct current (DC) because for DC:
options: The resistance of a capacitor is infinite
The dielectric between plates conducts DC
questions.solution:
For steady DC, frequency $f = 0$.
Capacitive reactance is $X_C = \frac{1}{2\pi f C} = \frac{1}{0} \to \infty$.
An infinite reactance presents an open circuit, blocking DC completely.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] A series LCR circuit with $L = 0.5\text{ H}$, $C = 8\,\mu\text{F}$, and $R = 10\,\Omega$ is connected to an AC source of variable frequency. The bandwidth $\Delta\omega$ of the circuit is:
questions.solution:
The bandwidth of an LCR resonant circuit is:
$$\Delta\omega = \frac{R}{L}$$
$$\Delta\omega = \frac{10\,\Omega}{0.5\text{ H}} = 20\text{ rad/s}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] An electrical device draws $2\text{ A}$ current from a $220\text{ V}$, $50\text{ Hz}$ AC line. If the current lags behind the voltage by $\pi/3$, the power consumed by the device is:
questions.solution:
Given $V_{\text{rms}} = 220\text{ V}$, $I_{\text{rms}} = 2\text{ A}$, and $\phi = \pi/3$:
$$P = V_{\text{rms}} I_{\text{rms}} \cos\phi = 220 \times 2 \times \cos\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right) = 440 \times 0.5 = 220\text{ W}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] In a series LCR circuit, the voltages across the inductor, capacitor, and resistor are measured to be $V_L = 80\text{ V}$, $V_C = 40\text{ V}$, and $V_R = 30\text{ V}$. The total applied RMS source voltage is:
questions.solution:
Using phasor addition for series LCR circuit:
$$V_{\text{source}} = \sqrt{V_R^2 + (V_L - V_C)^2}$$
$$V_{\text{source}} = \sqrt{30^2 + (80 - 40)^2} = \sqrt{30^2 + 40^2} = \sqrt{900 + 1600} = \sqrt{2500} = 50\text{ V}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] A choke coil is preferred over a rheostat in AC circuits to reduce current because:
options: Power loss in a choke coil is negligible
A choke coil increases the power factor
A choke coil completely blocks high voltage
A choke coil decreases the line voltage permanently
questions.solution:
An ideal choke coil has high inductance and nearly zero ohmic resistance.
Its power factor is $\cos\phi \approx 0$, meaning it introduces high reactance to restrict current with almost zero Joule heating loss, unlike a rheostat which dissipates energy as heat ($I^2 R$).

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] A capacitor of capacitance $C$ and an inductor of inductance $L$ form an LC resonant tank circuit. The oscillations of energy between electric and magnetic fields occur with angular frequency:
questions.solution:
Applying Kirchhoff's loop equation for an undamped LC circuit:
$$L \frac{d^2 q}{dt^2} + \frac{q}{C} = 0 \implies \frac{d^2 q}{dt^2} + \frac{1}{LC} q = 0$$
This is the standard SHM equation with natural angular frequency:
$$\omega_0 = \frac{1}{\sqrt{LC}}$$

questions.question: The peak value of an AC voltage supply of $220\text{ V}$ (mains supply) is approximately:
questions.solution:
Household rated supply specifies RMS voltage ($V_{\text{rms}} = 220\text{ V}$).
Peak voltage:
$$V_0 = \sqrt{2} V_{\text{rms}} = 1.4142 \times 220\text{ V} \approx 311.1\text{ V}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] In an ideal transformer, the primary winding has 500 turns and the secondary winding has 50 turns. If the input power to the primary is $1000\text{ W}$, the output power from the secondary is:
questions.solution:
An ideal transformer has $100\%$ efficiency, which means there are no core, copper, or hysteresis losses.
By conservation of energy:
$$P_{\text{out}} = P_{\text{in}} = 1000\text{ W}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2019] A pure inductor of $25.0\text{ mH}$ is connected to a source of $220\text{ V}$, $50\text{ Hz}$. The inductive reactance is (take $\pi = 3.14$):
questions.solution:
Inductive reactance:
$$X_L = 2\pi f L = 2 \times 3.1416 \times 50 \times (25.0 \times 10^{-3})$$
$$X_L = 100\pi \times 0.025 = 2.5\pi \approx 2.5 \times 3.1416 = 7.854\,\Omega \approx 7.85\,\Omega$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] A series LCR circuit has $L = 2.0\text{ H}$, $C = 32\,\mu\text{F}$, and $R = 10\,\Omega$. Find the resonant angular frequency $\omega_0$ in $\text{rad/s}$.
questions.solution:
Resonant angular frequency is given by:
$$\omega_0 = \frac{1}{\sqrt{LC}}$$
Substitute $L = 2.0\text{ H}$ and $C = 32 \times 10^{-6}\text{ F}$:
$$LC = 2.0 \times 32 \times 10^{-6} = 64 \times 10^{-6}\text{ s}^2$$
$$\sqrt{LC} = 8 \times 10^{-3}\text{ s}$$
$$\omega_0 = \frac{1}{8 \times 10^{-3}} = \frac{1000}{8} = 125.0\text{ rad/s}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] A coil has an inductance of $0.7\text{ H}$ and is joined in series with a resistance of $220\,\Omega$. When an alternating emf of $220\text{ V}$ at $50\text{ Hz}$ is applied to it, find the RMS current (in Amperes) in the circuit (take $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$, rounded to two decimal places).
questions.solution:
Inductive reactance:
$$X_L = 2\pi f L = 2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times 50 \times 0.7 = 2 \times 22 \times 5 = 220\,\Omega$$
Impedance:
$$Z = \sqrt{R^2 + X_L^2} = \sqrt{220^2 + 220^2} = 220\sqrt{2}\,\Omega$$
RMS current:
$$I_{\text{rms}} = \frac{V_{\text{rms}}}{Z} = \frac{220}{220\sqrt{2}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \approx 0.707\text{ A} \approx 0.71\text{ A}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] A step-down transformer has an efficiency of $80\%$. It reduces $200\text{ V}$ to $20\text{ V}$. If the output current is $4\text{ A}$, find the input current (in Amperes).
questions.solution:
Output power:
$$P_{\text{out}} = V_s I_s = 20\text{ V} \times 4\text{ A} = 80\text{ W}$$
Efficiency is $\eta = 0.80$:
$$P_{\text{in}} = \frac{P_{\text{out}}}{\eta} = \frac{80}{0.80} = 100\text{ W}$$
Input current:
$$I_p = \frac{P_{\text{in}}}{V_p} = \frac{100\text{ W}}{200\text{ V}} = 0.5\text{ A}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] In a series LCR circuit, $R = 10\,\Omega$, $L = 100\text{ mH}$, and $C = 1\,\mu\text{F}$. Find the Quality factor $Q$ of the circuit.
questions.solution:
Quality factor formula:
$$Q = \frac{1}{R}\sqrt{\frac{L}{C}}$$
Substitute $R = 10\,\Omega$, $L = 0.1\text{ H}$, and $C = 10^{-6}\text{ F}$:
$$\frac{L}{C} = \frac{0.1}{10^{-6}} = 10^5$$
$$\sqrt{\frac{L}{C}} = \sqrt{10^5} = 100\sqrt{10} \approx 100 \times 3.16227 = 316.23$$
$$Q = \frac{316.23}{10} = 31.62$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] An AC source of $V = 100\sqrt{2}\sin(100t)\text{ V}$ is connected to a series combination of a capacitor $C = 100\,\mu\text{F}$ and a resistor $R = 100\,\Omega$. Find the peak current (in Amperes) in the circuit (take $\sqrt{2} = 1.414$, rounded to one decimal place).
questions.solution:
Angular frequency: $\omega = 100\text{ rad/s}$.
Capacitive reactance:
$$X_C = \frac{1}{\omega C} = \frac{1}{100 \times (100 \times 10^{-6})} = \frac{1}{10^{-2}} = 100\,\Omega$$
Impedance:
$$Z = \sqrt{R^2 + X_C^2} = \sqrt{100^2 + 100^2} = 100\sqrt{2}\,\Omega$$
Peak voltage is $V_0 = 100\sqrt{2}\text{ V}$.
Peak current:
$$I_0 = \frac{V_0}{Z} = \frac{100\sqrt{2}}{100\sqrt{2}} = 1.0\text{ A}$$
